summary: Docked Dell Precision receives mismatched NVIDIA driver during imaging, breaking container runtime (nvidia-container-toolkit)
description: Multiple docked Dell Precision 7770 workstations imaged via the standard SCCM/Autopilot pipeline boot into Windows correctly but container workloads that depend on the NVIDIA GPU fail to start. Investigation shows the nvidia-container-toolkit (and underlying NVIDIA driver) bundled by the imaging job does not match the firmware/driver expected when the WD22TB4 dock is attached at first boot, resulting in Docker + containerd errors and inability to launch CUDA-enabled containers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start with factory-fresh Dell Precision 7770 and WD22TB4 dock connected via TB4
2) PXE boot / SCCM task sequence + our standard imaging task (image v2026.03.01) applied
3) OOBE completes, company policies and drivers installed by driver-management role
4) User logs in, Docker + containerd auto-start; attempt to run a simple CUDA container (e.g., nvidia/cuda:11.8-base)
5) Observe container fails to start with NVML/nvidia-smi errors and container runtime messages about missing driver hooks
logs: Mar 10 09:12:45 host1 dockerd[1234]: time="2026-03-10T09:12:45Z" level=error msg="Failed to start container: runtime error: driver hook not found"
Mar 10 09:12:45 host1 containerd[987]: level=error msg="nvidia-container-toolkit: failed to prepare device: NVML library not found"

Mar 10 09:12:46 host1 kernel: nvidia: module license 'NVIDIA' taints kernel
Mar 10 09:12:46 host1 kernel: nvidia 0000:01:00.0: firmware: failed to load nvidia/firmware.bin (-2)
investigation_notes: Reproduced on 3 distinct devices that were docked during first-boot after imaging; undocked systems do not show the failure.

Driver-management recipe currently applies NVIDIA driver package v525.85 from driver-factory repo; however dock firmware query shows TB4 dock exposing a different PCI topology requiring a newer 531-series driver.

Hypothesis: imaging job bundles driver packages in a fixed order and when TB4 is present at first boot Windows Device Install chooses the wrong driver (older package) because the dock enumerates GPU differently. This mismatched driver prevents NVML-init causing nvidia-container-toolkit to fail.
Checked SCCM task sequence: 'apply-drivers' step is non-idempotent and does not re-run after dock enumeration changes — potential race between driver package application and dock attaching.
Temporary repro: force uninstall NVIDIA drivers and re-install 531.* and containers recover immediately (worked on two test units).
comments: Support (Avery Chen) 2026-03-10: Customer-facing devs reported CI runners on docked laptops failing unit tests that use GPU. Created ticket after triage.
SRE (Marcus Patel) 2026-03-11: Confirmed logs; reproduced locally on eu-west lab with a docked 7770. Captured full driver store listing and attached to GH PR for driver-selection change.

Driver team (Lucia Fernandez) 2026-03-11: Asked for exact driver-store manifest and SCCM package GUIDs. Noted that 531-series package was published last week to driver-factory but imaging still picks up 525 due to package order in task sequence.
Imaging (Rohit Desai) 2026-03-12: Added a diagnostic step to re-enumerate PnP and re-run 'apply-drivers' post-firstboot for test run; will try with 10 machines in staging tomorrow.
Reporter (Avery Chen) 2026-03-12: Confirmed workaround (manual driver re-install) restored container workloads for two affected engineers; request for a systematic fix to avoid repeated manual steps.
resolution: Workaround: Manual uninstall of older NVIDIA driver and install of 531.* driver restores NVML and allows nvidia-container-toolkit to operate. Short-term mitigation: imaging team will add a post-OOBE driver re-enumeration + driver re-apply step for docked devices in the task sequence (testing in staging). Long-term: driver-management will update the driver-selection logic to prefer the dock-aware 531-series package when a TB4 dock is present and publish a patched ansible-imaging role. Tracking PRs: ansible-imaging/pull/312 (diagnostic step) and driver-factory/pull/89 (prefer 531). Follow-up required: schedule delayed rollout and update provisioning runbooks on Confluence.
